open_points.subject: ownership of staff login-email behavior
open_points.text: `staff_identity` owns “Email normalization” and “the administrative recovery override, the one replacement of a login email (A10)”, and is A10’s primary owner, but its Must not own section says “Email of any kind (there is none, A10)”.
open_points.question: Does “Email of any kind” prohibit only email messaging/challenge/delivery behavior, or also the login-email normalization, uniqueness, lookup, verified-mark, and replacement behavior assigned to `staff_identity`?
options: The prohibition means email messaging, challenges and delivery only; `staff_identity` owns login-email identity behavior.
The prohibition includes login-email behavior, which therefore needs another owner or removal.
open_points.default_guess: Interpret the prohibition as applying only to email messaging, challenges and delivery.

witness.initial: An active staff account uses normalized login email A; normalized email B is unused.
events: An administrator invokes the recovery override to replace A with B.
The account holder attempts to log in using B.
outcomes: Reading “Email of any kind” literally, `staff_identity` cannot normalize, check uniqueness, replace, or later resolve B; no permitted module owns the operation’s email behavior.
Reading it as shorthand for messaging and challenges, `staff_identity` normalizes and uniquely stores B, sets the recorded mark, and login with B succeeds.
witness.observer: The administrator and staff holder through the recovery and login API responses.
